column4:
This class comprises strings or codes assigned to instances of E1 CRM Entity in order to identify them
uniquely and permanently within the context of one or more organisations. Such codes are often known
as inventory numbers, registration codes, etc. and are typically composed of alphanumeric sequences.
The class E42 Identifier is not normally used for machine-generated identifiers used for automated
processing unless these are also used by human agents
column5:
This class comprises signs, either meaningful or not, or arrangements of signs following a specific
syntax, that are used or can be used to refer to and identify a specific instance of some class or category
within a certain context.
Instances of E41 Appellation do not identify things by their meaning, even if they happen to have one,
but instead by convention, tradition, or agreement. Instances of E41 Appellation are cultural constructs;
as such, they have a context, a history, and a use in time and space by some group of users. A given
instance of E41 Appellation can have alternative forms, i.e., other instances of E41 Appellation that are
always regarded as equivalent independent from the thing it denotes.
Specific subclasses of E41 Appellation should be used when instances of E41 Appellation of a
characteristic form are used for particular objects. Instances of E49 Time Appellation, for example,
which take the form of instances of E50 Date, can be easily recognised
column6:
This class comprises concepts denoted by terms from thesauri and controlled vocabularies used to
characterize and classify instances of CRM classes. Instances of E55 Type represent concepts in
contrast to instances of E41 Appellation which are used to name instances of CRM classes.
E55 Type is the CRM’s interface to domain specific ontologies and thesauri. These can be represented
in the CRM as subclasses of E55 Type, forming hierarchies of terms, i.e. instances of E55 Type linked
via P127 has broader term (has narrower term). Such hierarchies may be extended with additional
properties
column7:
This class comprises identifiers employed, or understood, by communication services to direct
communications to an instance of E39 Actor. These include E-mail addresses, telephone numbers, post
office boxes, Fax numbers, URLs etc. Most postal addresses can be considered both as instances of
E44 Place Appellation and E51 Contact Point. In such cases the subclass E45 Address should be used. URLs are addresses used by machines to access another machine through an http request. Since the
accessed machine acts on behalf of the E39 Actor providing the machine, URLs are considered as
instances of E51 Contact Point to that E39 Actor.

column9:
This class comprises institutions or groups of people that have obtained a legal recognition as a group
and can act collectively as agents.
This means that they can perform actions, own property, create or destroy things and can be held
collectively responsible for their actions like individual people. The term 'personne morale' is often
used for this in French
column10:
This class comprises any sort of name, number, code or symbol characteristically used to identify an E39 Actor.
An E39 Actor will typically have more than one E82 Actor Appellation, and instances of E82 Actor
Appellation in turn may have alternative representations. The distinction between corporate and
personal names, which is particularly important in library applications, should be made by explicitly
linking the E82 Actor Appellation to an instance of either E21 Person or E74 Group/E40 Legal Body.
If this is not possible, the distinction can be made through the use of the P2 has type mechanism

Dates may vary in their degree of precision.

column13:
This class comprises identifiers expressed in coding systems for places, such as postal addresses used
for mailing.
An E45 Address can be considered both as the name of an E53 Place and as an E51 Contact Point for
an E39 Actor. This dual aspect is reflected in the multiple inheritance. However, some forms of mailing addresses, such as a postal box, are only instances of E51 Contact Point, since they do not identify any
particular Place. These should not be documented as instances of E45 Address
column14:
This class comprises extents in space, in particular on the surface of the earth, in the pure sense of
physics: independent from temporal phenomena and matter.
The instances of E53 Place are usually determined by reference to the position of “immobile” objects
such as buildings, cities, mountains, rivers, or dedicated geodetic marks. A Place can be determined by combining a frame of reference and a location with respect to this frame. It may be identified by one or
more instances of E44 Place Appellation.
It is sometimes argued that instances of E53 Place are best identified by global coordinates or absolute
reference systems. However, relative references are often more relevant in the context of cultural
documentation and tend to be more precise. In particular, we are often interested in position in relation
to large, mobile objects, such as ships. For example, the Place at which Nelson died is known with
reference to a large mobile object – H.M.S Victory. A resolution of this Place in terms of absolute
coordinates would require knowledge of the movements of the vessel and the precise time of death,
either of which may be revised, and the result would lack historical and cultural relevance.
Any object can serve as a frame of reference for E53 Place determination. The model foresees the
notion of a "section" of an E19 Physical Object as a valid E53 Place determination

strings, bitmaps, vector graphics, etc.
E62 String is not further elaborated upon within the model
column17:
This class comprises people, either individually or in groups, who have the potential to perform intentional actions of kinds for which someone may be held responsible.  (Definition of the CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model version 6.2)
 
The CRM does not attempt to model the inadvertent actions of such actors. Individual people should be documented as instances of E21 Person, whereas groups should be documented as instances of either E74 Group or its subclass E40 Legal Body.
 
Examples:
London and Continental Railways (E40)
the Governor of the Bank of England in 1975 (E21)
Sir Ian McKellan (E21)

column4: A unique identifier assigned to each resource. Format: ACT-8-digit number (e.g. ACT-00000003).
column5: The name the actor is generally referred to as. An entry can have multiple name values with different name types - e.g. a person may have a primary name they are referred to as and an alternative name.
column6: The type of the name recorded in the "Name" field - e.g. Primary name, Alternative name, Local name. An actor can have several names, each with its own name type (e.g. a person may be referred to by a primary name and an alternative name).
column7: Information related to how the individual can be contacted. This can be either email, cellular phone, landline telephone, etc.
column8: The type of actor which this resource represents - e.g. a member of the MAEASaM team (a type of person), or a museum (a type of institution). Controlled by a hierarchical thesaurus (only certain values valid).
column9: Whether this actor is associated with another actor, and which actor it is associated with.
column10: The type of association the actor had with the other actor.
column11: This records the date at which the actor became associated with the other actor.
column12: This records the date at which the actor ended its association with the other actor.
column13: A text description of the location of this actor - for institutions this might be the address of the institution, or for people this might be where they are based professionally (not personal addresses). This does not need to be extremely detailed (or even included at all) if details cannot be provided or if an actor does not want to provide them.
column14: The name of the country in which the actor is physically situated.
column15: The coordinates (WGS 84 format) of the place indicated by the address.
column16: A basic description of the nature of the actor, if this is considered useful.
column17: The name of the individual responsible for creating the resource record.
column18: Any additional information relevant to this resource that the recorder feels should be documented.
column19: The date on which the resource record was created in the database.
column20: The name of the individual that uploaded this resource record to Arches.
column21: The date on which this resource record was added to Arches.
column22: The most recent date on which the resource record was modified.

column4: Identifiant unique attribué à chaque ressource saisie.
column5: Le nom sous lequel l'acteur est généralement désigné. Une entrée peut avoir plusieurs valeurs de nom avec différents types de nom - par exemple, une personne peut avoir un nom principal sous lequel elle est désignée et un nom alternatif.
column6: Le type du nom enregistré dans le champ « Name » - par exemple Primary name, Alternative name, Local name. Un acteur peut avoir plusieurs noms, chacun avec son propre type de nom (par exemple, une personne peut être désignée par un nom principal et un nom alternatif).
column7: Informations permettant de contacter la personne. Il peut s'agir d'une adresse électronique, d'un téléphone portable, d'un téléphone fixe, etc.
column8: Le type d'acteur que cette ressource représente - par exemple, un membre de l'équipe MAEASaM (un type de personne), ou un musée (un type d'institution). Contrôlé par un thésaurus hiérarchique (seules certaines valeurs sont valables)
column9: Indique si cet acteur est associé à un autre acteur, et à quel acteur il est associé.
column10: Le type d'association que l'acteur a eu avec l'autre acteur.
column11: Enregistre la date à laquelle l'acteur a été associé à l'autre acteur.
column12: Enregistre la date à laquelle l'acteur a mis fin à son association avec l'autre acteur.
column13: Une description textuelle de la localisation de cet acteur - pour les institutions, il peut s'agir de l'adresse de l'institution, ou pour les personnes, il peut s'agir de l'endroit où elles sont basées professionnellement (pas d'adresse personnelle). Il n'est pas nécessaire que cette description soit extrêmement détaillée (ni même qu'elle soit incluse du tout) si les détails ne peuvent pas être fournis ou si l'acteur ne souhaite pas les fournir.
column14: Le nom du pays dans lequel l'acteur est physiquement situé.
column15: Les coordonnées (format WGS 84) du lieu indiqué par l'adresse
column16: Une description de base de la nature de l'acteur, si cela est jugé utile.
column17: Le nom de la personne responsable de la création de l'enregistrement de la ressource.
column18: Tout commentaire supplémentaire nécessaire à la description complète de cet acteur ou de son entrée ici
column19: La date à laquelle l'enregistrement de la ressource a été créé dans la base de données.
column20: Le nom de la personne ayant téléversé cet enregistrement de ressource dans Arches.
column21: La date à laquelle cet enregistrement de ressource a été ajouté dans Arches.
column22: La date la plus récente à laquelle l'enregistrement de la ressource a été modifié.

column4: معرّف فريد يُسند إلى كل مورد. الصيغة: ACT متبوعًا برقم من 8 خانات (مثال: ACT-00000003).
column5: الاسم الذي تُعرف به الجهة الفاعلة عادةً. يمكن أن يتضمن السجل عدة أسماء بأنواع أسماء مختلفة - على سبيل المثال، قد يكون للشخص اسم رئيسي يُعرف به واسم بديل.
column6: نوع الاسم المسجّل في حقل "Name" - مثل Primary name وAlternative name وLocal name. يمكن أن يكون للجهة الفاعلة عدة أسماء، لكل منها نوع اسم خاص به (مثلًا قد يُشار إلى شخص باسم رئيسي واسم بديل).
column7: معلومات حول كيفية التواصل مع الشخص، مثل البريد الإلكتروني أو الهاتف المحمول أو الهاتف الأرضي وغيرها.
column8: نوع الجهة الفاعلة التي يمثلها هذا المورد - مثل عضو في فريق MAEASaM (نوع من الأشخاص) أو متحف (نوع من المؤسسات). يُضبط بواسطة مكنز هرمي (تُقبل قيم محددة فقط).
column9: ما إذا كانت هذه الجهة الفاعلة مرتبطة بجهة فاعلة أخرى، وما هي الجهة المرتبطة بها.
column10: نوع الارتباط الذي كان للجهة الفاعلة مع الجهة الفاعلة الأخرى.
column11: يسجّل التاريخ الذي أصبحت فيه الجهة الفاعلة مرتبطة بالجهة الفاعلة الأخرى.
column12: يسجّل التاريخ الذي أنهت فيه الجهة الفاعلة ارتباطها بالجهة الفاعلة الأخرى.
column13: وصف نصي لموقع هذه الجهة الفاعلة - بالنسبة للمؤسسات قد يكون عنوان المؤسسة، وبالنسبة للأشخاص قد يكون مكان عملهم المهني (وليس العنوان الشخصي). لا يلزم أن يكون هذا الوصف مفصلًا للغاية (أو حتى أن يُدرج أصلًا) إذا تعذّر تقديم التفاصيل أو إذا لم ترغب الجهة الفاعلة في تقديمها.
column14: اسم البلد الذي تقع فيه الجهة الفاعلة فعليًا.
column15: إحداثيات المكان المشار إليه في العنوان (بصيغة WGS 84).
column16: وصف أساسي لطبيعة الجهة الفاعلة، إذا اعتُبر ذلك مفيدًا.
column17: اسم الشخص المسؤول عن إنشاء سجل المورد.
column18: أي معلومات إضافية ذات صلة بهذا المورد يرى المسجّل أنه ينبغي توثيقها.
column19: التاريخ الذي أُنشئ فيه سجل المورد في قاعدة البيانات.
column20: اسم الشخص الذي رفع سجل المورد هذا إلى Arches.
column21: التاريخ الذي أُضيف فيه سجل المورد هذا إلى Arches.
column22: أحدث تاريخ عُدّل فيه سجل المورد.

column4: Identificador único atribuído a cada recurso. Formato: ACT seguido de um número de 8 dígitos (por exemplo, ACT-00000003).

column7: Informações sobre a forma de contactar a pessoa. Pode tratar-se de correio eletrónico, telemóvel, telefone fixo, etc.
column8: O tipo de ator que este recurso representa - por exemplo, um membro da equipa MAEASaM (um tipo de pessoa) ou um museu (um tipo de instituição). Controlado por um tesauro hierárquico (apenas determinados valores são válidos).

Esta descrição não precisa de ser muito detalhada (nem sequer incluída) se não for possível fornecer os dados ou se o ator não os quiser fornecer.
column14: O nome do país onde o ator está fisicamente situado.
column15: As coordenadas (formato WGS 84) do local indicado pelo endereço.
column16: Uma descrição básica da natureza do ator, caso se considere útil.

column21: A data em que este registo do recurso foi adicionado ao Arches.
